mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.2% in the month preceding the decision date predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to investor risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.22 in the month prior to decision_date
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when inflation surprise > 0.2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS (labor market tightness) and UNRATE (unemployment rate) above historical averages in the same month is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as a sign of labor market resilience and growth momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 148800 AND UNRATE > 3.5 in the same month
regime_hint: recovering labor market with low unemployment and rising hiring
failure_condition: Across 20 non-overlapping 60-day windows, the interaction shows no significant positive effect on 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% signals supply-side weakness that precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: early-stage soft landing turning into contraction
failure_condition: In 10 consecutive 5-day windows with INDPRO decline > 2%, no negative 5-day forward returns are observed (empirical frequency < 30%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (housing starts) for three consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as a leading indicator of consumer spending restraint.
regime_hint: early signs of a cooling housing market
failure_condition: During 10 such 3-month HOUST declines, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in more than 70% of cases (frequency test).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, the S&P 500 exhibits negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market pricing of higher policy costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous_month_value + 0.25 in the current month
regime_hint: sharp increase in the federal funds rate
failure_condition: In 50 such FEDFUNDS hikes, the 5-day forward return is never negative (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in UNRATE below 3.5% and a rise in PAYEMS above 150,000 in the same month signals a tight labor market that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 AND PAYEMS > 150000 in the same month
regime_hint: labor market tightening in a growth environment
failure_condition: Across 30 such triggered months, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in GDPC1 (GDP chained price parity) of at least 3% predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as a signal of economic softening.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous_month_value - 3 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20 such two-month GDPC1 declines, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 40% of cases (frequency test).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary tightening (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 shows positive forward returns over the next 20 days as markets anticipate a near-term rate cut.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5 AND FEDFUNDS > previous_month_value in the current month
failure_condition: In 10 such tightening regimes, the 20-day forward return is never positive (p-value > 0.05).
